rationale: This is a direct rediscovery of the well-documented gross-profitability-plus-value composite (Novy-Marx 2013 combined with HML / Asness-Frazzini "quality at a reasonable price"), and multiplying two uniform [0,1] ranks is dominated by their average, so the claimed pure-interaction content is largely illusory.

The INDICATOR gate assigns roughly half the sample an exact value of zero, which is not "off" but is instead placed above every profitable firm with negative earnings yield — degenerate breakpoints and a ranking that contradicts the stated distress story.

Since rank(P/B) is monotonically the complement of rank(B/M), this difference of ranks is exactly an equal-weighted additive value+profitability composite, so the "disagreement measure, not a relabeled value or quality score" reasoning is internally false and the signal duplicates proposal 1.

Conditioning value on the five-year slope of ROA rather than its level is a defensible value-trap-versus-recovery distinction that is not a standard published anomaly, though the rank-product form again behaves mostly additively and the slow-moving trend may dilute the effect.

Gross-profits-to-enterprise-value is itself a published anomaly (Novy-Marx 2013), the raw unranked ratio will dominate the [0,1] margin-rank multiplier so the "interaction" is cosmetic, and negative or near-zero enterprise values will produce sign-flipping outliers.

Internally consistent (product of two positively oriented ranks with a correctly negative expected sign) and usefully aimed at the short leg, but note that price-to-sales deflated by margin is approximately price-to-earnings, so it risks partially recovering the classic earnings-yield effect.
